purpose: score the merged Qwen3-1.7B distillation and base Qwen3-1.7B on the F8 210-item ladder (accept/revert gate before LPM retraining)

harness.protocol_source: benchmark-workspace/evaluate.py (SYSTEM_PROMPT, PROMPT_TEMPLATE, extract_answer imported, not duplicated)

inference.transport: rlm_slice.model_host.ModelHost (4-bit NF4, full_precision=False default; unchanged since #116)

harness_fidelity_check.description: re-ran the F8 0.6B-distill row on today's stack to confirm the invocation reproduces F8
harness_fidelity_check.note: 1-item net difference on the 4-bit path; far below every effect reported here

vs_f8_0.6B_distillation.finding: statistically identical; adapted 1.7B matches, does not beat, the 0.6B distillation

capacity_baseline.note: raw adaption margin at 1.7B is smaller because the base starts 30 pp higher

go_reasons: 1.7B distillation clearly beats 1.7B base: +13.8 pp (0.8667 vs 0.7286), McNemar p=9.0e-06, non-overlapping Wilson CIs
adaptation therefore demonstrably landed; the distilled-0.6B vs raw-1.7B confound from #231 is removed
hard tier (F8's decisive tier) rises +27.3 pp (0.3939 -> 0.6667)
caveats: the 1.7B lift (+13.8 pp) is about one-third of F8's 0.6B lift (+44.3 pp) in raw pp; base 1.7B already scores +30 pp over base 0.6B
the adapted 1.7B matches, not beats, the 0.6B distillation (0.8667 vs 0.8714, p=1.00); Phase 4/5 should not be sold as a ladder-quality gain
